text.text: The company's operating view in one place: customers and their renewal dates, the roadmap and who asked for what, support tickets and the monthly numbers. Start every Monday with the Dashboard and the At risk view. Log a ticket the moment a customer asks, and link it to the roadmap item it is about.

text.text: Thirty minutes every Monday keeps a small company honest. Same agenda, same order.
Agenda
Metrics: open the Dashboard and read last month's row aloud.
Customers: walk through At risk and Renewing in the next 14 days.
Support: any ticket older than two days and anything marked High.
Roadmap: what shipped, what is in build, what is stuck.
Decisions: write each decision in the weekly notes with an owner and date.
Rules
No new roadmap items added during the review.
Anything over 5 minutes of discussion becomes its own meeting.
The meeting ends with three things nobody has to ask about again.
Churn rarely arrives as a surprise. The signals are usually there weeks before the cancellation email.
Signals of trouble

cells.text: The tool is not part of their routine
Fix the bug, then call personally
The team is shrinking or switching
Ask about the business, not the product
Renewal in 30 days with no contact

text.text: When a customer cancels
Press Flag at risk early, not after the email.
Ask what would have changed their mind and write it on the customer row.
Thank them and leave the door open.
A roadmap is a list of bets, ranked. The ranking should be something you can defend in two sentences.
Questions to ask
How many customers asked, and how much revenue do they represent?
Does it make the next sale easier?
How big is it, honestly?
What do we stop doing to make room?
Process
Link every request ticket to a roadmap item.
Review asks and size each month.
Move items to Planned only when someone owns them.
Tell the customers who asked when it ships.
